video.title: Open Source, Faster Jev is HERE

protocol.status: v2 labeler B (rubric v2), independent of A
protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Whisper small transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Someone used browser-use plus Jev (ASR: 'Jeff') to book flights; hook is the concrete use, payoff is 'the entire booking took seven seconds and cost $0.0039', closed by what it actually did (opens Google Flights, picks dates, finds cheapest). Opens on 'some other folks', a mild back-reference, but nothing needed is lost.

Hot take: Leia is less accurate than Jev, but Jev took three years in stealth and an open-weights clone appeared within a week; lands on 'the future is bright for open source' at 422.3. Ending right on the 'cloned it in five days or a week' line (416.1) also works.

Question hook 'what the heck is System 1?' answered via Thinking Fast and Slow: System 2 is slow/logical like today's LLMs, System 1 is fast/instinctive, which is where Jev and Leia come from. Stops before the long example list read off the screen.

also_ok.why: Cold open: an AI playing Snake locally at ~30 decisions/sec, then what Leia is (a System 1 classification model, decisions in under 33 ms). Relies partly on the on-screen Snake game, hence also_ok.

Wider version of the flight clip: 'people have been doing all sorts of things with it' -- Mario in real time, lead scoring, then the 7-second $0.0039 flight booking. Mario bit leans on the screen and the lead-scoring bit is garbled.
Running open-weights Leia locally is faster than the Jev API; he asked Claude Code to port the demo to Leia and it one-shot it in a single session. Opens on 'But what's even cooler', a mild run-up.

Playground walkthrough of how a Jev question works (state, question, criteria), answered with 'hamburger is a sandwich: 94% true' and 'avocado toast: 94% false'. Screen-shared and too long to cut under 75s without losing the setup.

negatives.why: 'Watch this, it's gonna be so fast' -- live narration of the browser agent clicking through Google Flights; the point is entirely on screen.
Email-classification example read off the screen: 94% confidence, 39 ms, 'three times faster than Jev'. Numbers sound clippable but depend on the display.
'So yeah' list of Kev model sizes (9B, 4B, 0.8B, open weights) -- numbers and a strong 'it's so good', but a run-on list with no point of its own.
